blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-2 (Failed and dropped deliveries are invisible to operators) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Wait between attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (for example 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s), and retry only on network errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx — not on other 4xx responses, which will not succeed on a retry. The loop is bounded and the POST is safe to repeat (merchants deduplicate by `x-event-id`), but the attempts are not spaced: when a merchant's server restarts or returns 503 for a few seconds, the five attempts are spent within that window (instantly on fast 5xx responses) and the event is dropped, while an overloaded merchant gets hit five times in a row. As `publish` in `src/events.ts` awaits each listener in turn, the retries also hold the payment service's call for up to 25 s per event; spacing them out makes that worse, so move delivery off the publish path (a queue or a background job) when adding the backoff.
findings.title: Webhook retries fire back to back, with no backoff

findings.recommendation: Log through the project's structured `logger` (`src/logger.ts`, as `src/events.ts` does) rather than `console.debug`: a `warn` per failed attempt with `eventId`, `attempt`, the HTTP `status` or the error, and an `error` when the event is dropped, with `eventId`, the merchant id and the payment id; add a counter of dropped deliveries an operator can alert on. Today a merchant whose endpoint returns 500 gets no attempt logged at all (a non-ok response falls through without any log), the final drop is a free-text debug line that production log levels filter out, and the `false` returned by `deliver` is ignored by the listener at line 34 — so a payment webhook is lost permanently with nothing for the operator or the merchant support team to see.
findings.title: Failed and dropped deliveries are invisible to operators
